To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
inattention and/or hyperactivity/impulsive behavior is associated with less weight loss after treatment for pediatric obesity.
the HI score of the Strengths Difficulty Questionnaire predicts short- and long- term weight loss in overweight and obese children and adolescents.

inattention and/or hyperactivity/impulsive symptoms are linearly associated (i.e. a higher score predicts less) with short- and longer term weight loss in overweight and obese children and adolescents treated as outpatients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of inattention and impulsivity in the context of weight loss.
the question, whether the degree of inattention and/or hyperactivity/impusivity in overweight children and adolescents can be used as a prognostic indicator for the success of weight loss programs.
the role of inattention and/or hyperactivity in weight loss and weight maintenance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

inattention and/or hyperactivity/impulse control problems are associated with less weight loss in overweight and obese children and adolescents, and that these children may benefit from additional support during treatment and follow-up.
HI predicts weight loss in overweight and obese children and adolescents, but the effect is rather small.
inattentiveness and hyperactivity are linearly associated to reduced short- and longer term weight loss.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HI subscale of the SDQ can be used as an additional predictor for weight loss and maintenance of treatment outcome in overweight children and adolescents.

inattention and/or hyperactivity/impulivity are associated with reduced weight loss and maintenance of weight loss in obese and overweight children and adolescents treated in multidisciplinary treatment centers.
the hyperactivity/inattentiveness of children with obesity can be a barrier for successful weight loss and weight loss maintenance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inattention and impulsivity/hyperactivity should be addressed in treatment of childhood and adolescent obesity.
inattention and/or hyperactivity/impulsive behaviors are negatively associated with weight loss and long-term weight maintenance.
children and adolescents who are inattentive and hyperactive/impulsive have a harder time with weight loss and maintenance.
